answer: Chronological work ledger. Each identity must contribute verifiably useful outputs whose timestamps form an unbroken spiral of daily activity; a gap decays the record. Peers counter-sign entries, and a fresh identity cannot buy history, so every clone pays the full elapsed-time cost of rebuilding a continuous trail. Newcomers start in an isolated lagoon with limited reach until the ledger crosses a threshold. Only then does their signal propagate network-wide.
